articles.title: Mutual funds' Nifty 50 allocation falls to 21-year low in Q2
articles.excerpt:
Domestic mutual funds’ allocation to Nifty 50 stocks fell to a 21-year low in the September quarter, slipping below 50 per cent for the first time in over two decades, as fund portfolios continued to expand beyond the country’s largest benchmark companies.

The share of Nifty 50 stocks in mutual funds’ holdings of NSE-listed equities declined by two percentage points to 49.4 per cent from 51.4 per cent in June, according to the National Stock Exchange’s (NSE) India Ownership Tracker report. This was 13.5 percentage points below the December 2019 peak of 63 per cent.

articles.excerpt:

Small investors are becoming pickier about the stocks they own. In the September quarter, they reduced their stakes in nearly half of listed companies, even as Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank and PC Jeweller drew more retail shareholders.

A Mint analysis of 4,729 BSE-listed companies showed retail ownership (those holding up to ₹1 lakh in equity) declined in 49.4% of companies in Q2FY27, up from 47.5% in Q1FY27. The proportion recording an increase slipped to 42.4% from 43.2%, while 8.2% saw no change, according to ACE Equity data.
